handback.title: Thin install: no Dokima code in the adopter's repo
handback.summary: Adopters install one short workflow and a settings file; all Dokima code runs from Dokima's repo.
handback.feature: Dokima installs as one short workflow and a settings file. Stories: shared workflows, installer, README, wiki, first merge.

stories.title: Dokima's workflows run from Dokima's own repo
stories.user_story: An adopter's runs use Dokima's tagged code and the adopter's own secrets, failing clearly when one is missing.
stories.task: Make Dokima's workflows callable from another repo at a tag, take all code from Dokima's repo, and fail clearly on a missing bot or key.
stories.context: Today every workflow checks out the running repo and runs `python -m dokima` from it (`actions/checkout@v5` with no `repository:`), so an adopter must hold `dokima/`. Reusable workflows need `on: workflow_call`; `agent.yml` already has one. Environment secrets work in a called workflow when its job names `environment: keys`. Events such as `workflow_run` name workflows by their name in the adopter's repo, so one shared entry that routes by event keeps the adopter's file short. Role key secrets are already named in settings (`dokima/agents.py`, #794): prove it still holds when called from outside. The app id is `vars.DOKIMA_APP_ID` and its key `secrets.DOKIMA_APP_KEY` in every app-token step. Commits are authored as `${SLUG}[bot]` (`agent.yml:219`) and credit `co_author` (`agent.yml:474`). `playthrough.yml` and `wiki.yml` stay Dokima-only and are never shared. Default secret names stay today's (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`); the owner's `CLAUDE_TOKEN` is any name a repo sets. The owner wrote about 15 lines; 20 is the ceiling set here.
promises: Keys only in the keys environment
Missing bot or key fails with the fix
Co-author trailer on by default, can be turned off
Thin workflow calls shared workflows by tag

acceptance_criteria.text: A run on an adopter's repo takes all Dokima code from Dokima's own repo, never the adopter's.
acceptance_criteria.words: All Dokima code runs from Dokima's own repo inside GitHub Actions.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every job that reads a key takes it from the repo's keys environment, in the shared workflows too.
acceptance_criteria.words: Credentials** live only in GitHub secrets on the repo (the `keys` environment)

acceptance_criteria.text: Each role reads its model key from the secret its settings name.
acceptance_criteria.words: `settings.yaml` only names which secret each role reads.

acceptance_criteria.text: A run with no bot set up fails, and its message says how to set the bot up.
acceptance_criteria.words: Missing bot or key fails loudly with the fix in the message

acceptance_criteria.text: A run with no model key secret fails, and its message names the secret and how to add it.
acceptance_criteria.words: a run without the secret fails with a clear message

acceptance_criteria.text: Every commit Dokima makes carries a co-author line naming Dokima's bot by default.
acceptance_criteria.words: the trailer `Co-authored-by: dokima[bot]`, so Dokima appears in the contributor list of every repo it touches.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a repo's settings turn the co-author line off, its commits carry none.
acceptance_criteria.words: the adopter can turn it off in settings.

acceptance_criteria.text: The adopter's workflow calls Dokima's shared workflows at a release tag, never a branch.
acceptance_criteria.words: calls Dokima's shared workflows by tag.

acceptance_criteria.text: The adopter's workflow is at most 20 lines long.

stories.title: Installing adds only the workflow and settings
stories.user_story: Installing Dokima adds one short workflow and a settings file to a repo, and nothing else.
stories.task: Build the installer from the play-through's copy installer, writing only the thin workflow and settings file.
stories.context: `dokima/playthrough.py:161-223` (`install_files`, `Sandbox.install`) copies `dokima/` and every workflow; it is the starting point. The installed files are exactly `.github/workflows/dokima.yml` and `.dokima/settings.yaml`: no Python, no `playthrough.yml` or `wiki.yml`. The settings file names secrets only, never their values.
promises: Install adds only the workflow and settings

acceptance_criteria.text: Installing Dokima adds exactly two files to a repo: its one workflow and its settings file.
acceptance_criteria.words: install adds only the workflow and settings

acceptance_criteria.text: Installing writes no secret's value into any file it adds.

stories.title: README install steps use the thin workflow

stories.title: An empty repo reaches its first merge from the docs
stories.user_story: An owner with an empty repo gets to a first merged pull request with only the docs.
stories.task: Follow only the docs on a fresh empty repo until its first Dokima pull request merges.
stories.context: Needs real GitHub, so CI cannot prove it; see the question on the trial issue #746. A release tag must exist for the thin workflow to call (#755).
promises: An empty repo reaches its first merged PR using only the docs

acceptance_criteria.text: An empty repo reaches its first merged pull request following only the docs.
acceptance_criteria.words: an empty repo reaches its first merged PR using only the docs.

raises.label: Bot before shared app
raises.text: Until the shared app exists, should the co-author line name the repo's own bot? The plan assumes it does.
raises.evidence: `agent.yml:219` authors commits as the repo's own bot; the shared app is still open in #747.

raises.label: Your own credit
raises.text: Here, should Dokima's bot line replace your co-author credit? The plan assumes your line stays, since a repo's setting wins.
raises.evidence: `.dokima/settings.yaml` sets `co_author` to you, from #110; this issue says the trailer replaces it.

raises.label: First merge proof
raises.text: Should the trial issue prove the first merge from the docs? The plan keeps it here, checked by hand.
raises.evidence: It needs real GitHub; #775 says the plan check refuses a criterion with no test; #746 runs the trial.
